evidence: src/domain/errors.ts declares DomainError(kind: ErrorKind, message), the module's single error type.
src/domain/order.ts keeps the lifecycle rules in NEXT_STATE and CANCELLABLE, enforces them only in advance() and cancel(), and throws DomainError("conflict", ...).
src/domain/product.ts enforces the stock rule only in reserveStock() and throws DomainError("conflict", ...), the same way order.ts does.
The only imports inside the module go from order.ts and product.ts to errors.ts, so the files depend on one shared abstraction and do not copy logic between them.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The three files make up one coherent order-fulfilment domain model. errors.ts defines the shared error abstraction (DomainError with ErrorKind). order.ts owns the order lifecycle invariants: ORDER_STATES, NEXT_STATE and CANCELLABLE are each defined once and enforced only in advance and cancel. product.ts owns the stock invariant, enforced only in reserveStock. Both order.ts and product.ts raise rule violations through DomainError("conflict", ...), so neither bypasses the shared abstraction. No rule is copied between files, and nothing unrelated to the domain is mixed in. One small gap: neither reserveStock nor releaseStock checks that quantity is positive. That is a missing check, not a split, duplication or bypass, so it does not fail this rule.
